claims.exact_statement: Under the classical semi-infinite, constant-property Sand diffusion model with negligible initial interface resistance, tau^(-1/2)=2i/(sqrt(pi*D_eff)*c0*F), Qmax=i*tau, and VSC=i*Qmax=i^2*tau=pi*D_eff*c0^2*F^2/4.
assumptions: one-dimensional semi-infinite diffusion
constant D_eff and initial c0
uniform constant flux
initial interface resistance negligible
claims.status: source-reported; independently algebraically reconstructed; source equation verified
claims.novelty_boundary: Sand relation is established prior art; VSC is an algebraic reparameterization, not an independent measurement.
costs: D_eff and c0 must be measured or inferred for the same alloy, state, temperature, and protocol
the parameter fit and unit conversion must be disclosed
claims.falsifier: A dimensionally and algebraically inconsistent primary equation or a reproducible same-condition measurement inconsistent with the stated model would falsify use of this relation for that interface; neither was established here.
claims.next_gate: Clarify and independently reconstruct how the published Fig. 2f fit and Table 3 effective coefficient treat the nonzero regression intercept.

claims.exact_statement: Ji et al.'s abstract explicitly reports that phase-field modelling predicts electrolyte overpotential above a critical value after stripped capacity exceeds 70% of model full-depletion capacity; this is a model-scoped prediction, not a universal experimentally established law.
assumptions: the specific Ji phase-field model and parameter set
claims.status: source-reported; scope reconstructed from primary abstract and Supplementary Note 8
claims.novelty_boundary: No universal 70% threshold claim or falsification is made.
costs: model parameter, grid, contact, electrolyte, and critical-overpotential assumptions govern transfer
claims.falsifier: A primary article statement showing a different scope or a same-model rerun disproving the reported crossing would change this claim.
claims.next_gate: If testing transfer, measure overpotential/contact evolution in matched physical cells rather than treating the model fraction as a universal threshold.

claims.exact_statement: Publisher Fig. 2f source data contain eight LiMgLa and three LiMg raw depletion points. Reconstructed LiMgLa free-intercept fit has slope 0.0084508424 per mA cm^-2, intercept 0.0011772528 s^-1/2, R^2=0.9762727; forcing the fit through the origin gives slope 0.0092713730 and an inverse-square VSC of 1.163354e6 A^2 s m^-4. The source Table 3 LiMgLa VSC is 1.46e6 A^2 s m^-4.
assumptions: time in source data is hours and transformed using seconds
linear regressions use exactly the raw rows shown in the publisher XLSX
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a reanalysis of source data, not external validation or proof of a source error.
costs: no measurement uncertainty, replicates, or fit-selection rationale inferred
the free-intercept line is not the canonical Sand equation
claims.falsifier: Revised source data, a different disclosed regression protocol, or author-provided parameter provenance could resolve or supersede these fit values.
claims.next_gate: Reproduce the exact estimator that generated Table 3 D_eff and obtain raw replicate-level uncertainty.

claims.exact_statement: For independent semi-infinite diffusion columns with common constant D,c0, fixed nominal galvanostatic density jbar, and every local nonnegative flux bounded by j(x,t)<=kappa*jbar through the target time, no column depletes before VSC/(kappa^2*jbar^2); hence kappa^2*jbar*Q<VSC is a sufficient condition for avoiding Sand depletion up to nominal-area charge Q. Under a uniform active-area fraction alpha with all current through active contact, kappa=1/alpha and the sufficient global-current bound is jbar<VSC*alpha^2/Q_target.
assumptions: independent one-dimensional semi-infinite columns
same time-independent D and c0 at all locations
nonnegative flux
measured finite pointwise local-current amplification bound
no lateral transport or mechanical/electrolyte failure in the submodel
claims.novelty_boundary: The inequality is a comparison argument for a standard diffusion model; generic area/current localization is preempted by prior art.
costs: requires local-flux upper bound kappa, not only global current or global EIS
claims.falsifier: The mathematical statement fails if flux can exceed the assumed bound or if the assumed diffusion-column interface is not the operative model; physical prediction is falsified by same-cell tests where a validated model's sufficient bound is violated without the predicted depletion/failure criterion.
claims.next_gate: Acquire calibrated spatial upper-bound kappa(t) in same-condition cells and test the threshold at matched target current/capacity.

claims.exact_statement: Vema et al. report impurity-particle deposition at a stripping Li|LLZO interface and derive a critical capacity from particle spacing and creep under stack pressure; Supplementary Eqs. S18-S25 include a particle/pressure/current capacity model and initial-interface-resistance correction.
assumptions: nominally high-purity Li and LLZO source system
particle deposition model and Li creep law
uniform-layer idealization for the closed-form capacity; nonuniform patches require extra state
claims.novelty_boundary: The particle model is not a result for Mg/La inoculant or LLZTO.
costs: stack pressure, stripping rate, particle radius/fraction, initial resistance and Li creep parameters
claims.falsifier: Same-system microscopy and resistance/pressure experiments that contradict particle deposition/creep predictions would falsify that mechanism for the tested conditions.
claims.next_gate: Measure inclusion chemistry, conductivity, geometry, creep, and critical capacity in the candidate composition before transferring Eq. S25.

claims.exact_statement: Ji et al.'s Supplementary Fig. 13 presents Mg/La EDX maps at a LiMgLa|LLZTO interface after partial and full stripping; it does not quantify a continuous residue layer, inclusion fraction/size, or ionic conductivity.
assumptions: figure captions and shown maps correspond to cited partial/full stripping states
claims.novelty_boundary: Element maps establish species distribution only at their resolution; they do not show transport function.
costs: quantitative microscopy, conductivity/phase analysis, and replicated interface preparation required
claims.falsifier: No Mg/La-rich material at the interface under repeated protocol-matched stripping would falsify the proposed residue-state link.
claims.next_gate: Quantify residue coverage, radius distribution, connectivity, chemistry, and conductance before and after cycling.

claims.exact_statement: Candidate hypothesis: in LiMgLa|LLZTO cycling, the Mg/La-derived residue state could add a pressure- and history-dependent contact-loss/restart-resistance gate beyond VSC and local-current amplification; whether this happens is UNKNOWN.
assumptions: Mg/La-bearing phases persist or accumulate at the interface
their conductivity/creep/contact role differs measurably from bulk Li
initial impedance/current geometry can be matched across controls
claims.status: candidate hypothesis; untested; no claimed discovery
claims.novelty_boundary: Cross-source material transfer is the testable question; generic current constriction and impurity deposition are prior art.
costs: matched cell batches, replicated pressure/rate protocols, calibrated local-current maps, three-electrode impedance, destructive cryo-PFIB/SEM/EDS, independent D/c0 and creep acquisition
claims.falsifier: No residue, or no predictive contribution of residue descriptors to capacity/restart resistance after matching initial Z, pressure, and kappa, falsifies this hypothesis for the tested protocol.
claims.next_gate: Run blinded, preregistered pure-Li / Mg-only / Mg-La matched experiment with local-current, EIS, strip-rest-restart, and inclusion mapping.

claims.exact_statement: A generic novelty claim for local current amplification by shrinking contact is preempted by existing coupled void/current-hotspot modeling and current 2026 phase-field work on geometry, roughness, pressure, and current amplification.
assumptions: comparison based on primary papers and their explicit abstracts/model scope
claims.status: prior-art boundary; source-checked; no priority claim made
claims.novelty_boundary: No exhaustive priority search; conclusion is limited to generic current-localization framing.
costs: further literature search required before any public novelty assertion
claims.falsifier: Not applicable to a physical statement; a broader or narrower priority claim requires further source inspection.
claims.next_gate: Continue only on a distinct, composition-specific residue-state prediction after the matched-material mechanism survives.

claims.exact_statement: In the parallel-patch interface model, scalar total conductance G=I/V and global current I do not bound peak local amplification kappa without local-conductance/geometry constraints: for any active fraction alpha, assigning conductance G to area alpha*A preserves measured impedance Z=1/G while kappa=1/alpha.
assumptions: parallel local conductance patches under a common terminal voltage
insulating inactive interface
no lateral current redistribution in this counterexample model
claims.status: exact counterexample within a named interface model
claims.proof_path: proofs/conditional_contact_depletion_bound.md, section 'Why a scalar impedance does not identify kappa'
claims.novelty_boundary: This is an elementary identifiability counterexample, not a claim that real LLZTO cells obey the parallel-patch model.
costs: a real controller must separately acquire local conductance/current or validate geometric and constitutive bounds
claims.falsifier: A finite peak-flux bound derived from scalar G and I alone would contradict this counterexample only by adding a premise that rules out the constructed patch family.
claims.next_gate: Measure local flux or establish independent finite bounds on local conductance and geometry in the intended cell.
